title: A Quantitative Shadowing Lemma for Hyperbolic Operators
content: Let \(A\) be a bounded invertible hyperbolic operator on a complex Hilbert space. We compare its optimal two-sided shadowing constant \(S(A)\) with the hyperbolicity robustness radius \(r(A)\), the operator-norm distance to a perturbation whose spectrum meets the unit circle. We prove the dimension-independent estimate \[ \frac{1}{r(A)}\le S(A)\le \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{r(A)^3}\, \coth\!\left(\frac{\pi}{r(A)}\right)}. \] The exponent \(\frac{3}{2}\) as \(r(A)\downarrow0\) is optimal. It is attained in order by finite-dimensional matrices of uniformly bounded norm and by bilateral weighted shifts on \(\ell^2(Z)\). The latter have fixed spectrum \(\{z:|z|=\frac{1}{2}\}\), uniformly bounded norms and inverse norms, and an explicitly computable shadowing constant. The upper bound follows from the exact dual norm of the Green operator, Hilbert-valued Parseval identities, and the resolvent derivative formula.
